title: Deterministic request identity + KPI enrichment proxy for per-request attribution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a lightweight proxy that deterministically generates a stable request identity for each inference request and enriches OTLP/Prometheus metrics and traces with that identity. This enables accurate per-request KPI attribution (latency, token-cost, error-class) across the ingestion pipeline and downstream dashboards without relying on best-effort client-supplied IDs.
technical_approach: Deploy a sidecar/ingest-proxy that sits between edge load balancers and the inference runtime. For each request, the proxy will: 1) Compute a deterministic request_id using a canonicalized tuple (tenant_id, route_hash, request_nonce if present, client_ip fingerprint) salted with a per-deployment secret. 2) Attach request_id to OTLP spans and to metrics as a low-cardinality anchor label (request_identity_v1) and optionally a hashed_request_bin label for Prometheus rollups. 3) Respect sampling decisions: when traces are sampled out, still emit a lightweight anchor metric event with request_id to ensure KPI attribution for aggregated counts. 4) Use an LRU KV cache to dedupe and stabilize identities for retried requests. 5) Expose a small admin API for key rotation and rollout toggles. The proxy will be implemented in Rust for low CPU overhead and integrated into existing otlp/prometheus exporters via header injection and OTLP span attribute enrichment.
success_criteria: 1) >=99% of inference requests in staging have a request_identity_v1 label attached across OTLP and Prometheus paths. 2) Per-request KPI dashboards (latency, tokens, errors) show stable attributions with less than 1% orphaned metrics. 3) Proxy adds <1ms median latency and <2% p99 CPU increase on dedicated nodes. 4) No tenant-level cardinality explosion observed after 48h in canary tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy to 3 low-traffic tenants in staging with identity generation enabled and observability dashboards watching cardinality and orphan rate. Phase 2 (expanded canary): enable on a subset of Dedicated nodes across regions, monitor cost/latency. Phase 3 (gradual global): toggle on for all hosted API traffic while running a backfill job to patch historical KPI discrepancies on dashboards. Feature flag will allow fallback to client-supplied IDs or disabled mode.
risks: 1) Cardinatlity growth if request identity scheme is too granular; mitigated with hashed bins and TTL-based eviction. 2) Secret/key rotation causing identity mismatch and double-counting; mitigated by supporting overlapping key windows and marking identity_version. 3) Performance overhead in high-throughput paths; mitigated with Rust implementation and microbenchmarks. 4) Compliance concerns about deriving identity from IP — we will provide opt-out and tenant-configurable fingerprinting policies.
open_questions: Should request_id include model_version or is route_hash sufficient for attribution?
What minimum set of attributes should be canonicalized to avoid collisions while limiting cardinality?
Do we want to expose request_identity_v1 to customers in logs/console or keep it internal-only?
How to handle cross-service propagation when requests fan out to secondary helpers (rerankers, embeddings)?
